saints.name: St. Damien of Molokai
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: The Belgian missionary who gave his life to the abandoned lepers of Molokai and died one of them…
biography: Jozef De Veuster was born on 3 January 1840 at Tremelo in Belgium, a farmer's son. Entering the Congregation of the Sacred Hearts, he took the name Damien and, when his brother Pamphile fell too ill to sail, volunteered in his place for the Hawaiian mission; ordained at Honolulu in 1864, he labored nine years on the island of Hawaii.

In 1873 Bishop Maigret sought priests for Kalaupapa, the peninsula of Molokai to which the government exiled its lepers. Damien went with three companions and begged to stay when the others were relieved. For sixteen years he was priest, doctor, carpenter, and gravedigger to the outcasts, building houses and churches, dressing ulcers, and shaping coffins with his own hands.

In 1885 he greeted his flock with the words 'We lepers': he had taken the disease. He died at Kalaupapa on 15 April 1889, aged forty-nine, and his body was borne back to Louvain in 1936. Beatified in 1995 and canonized in 2009, he is the patron of lepers and outcasts, for he made himself one of them.
saints.knownFor: A life laid down for the lepers of Molokai.
